answer: Each agent must post a bond that is locked until its actions survive a challenge window; a verifier samples claims and can slash the bond when linked identities repeat the same fabricated evidence. Creating a terrace of fake accounts therefore requires separate capital for each identity, and detection burns that stake rather than merely banning a name. The attacker also pays the opportunity cost of locked funds, while honest agents can distinguish costly participation from cheap pigment and sable account churn.
